The 26-layer stack operates as a hierarchical Bayesian network where each layer refines contextual priors into actionable signals. L01 sets temporal anchors; L03 introduces baseline efficiencies; L06 incorporates environmental modifiers. Each layer's output forms a conditional probability distribution that feeds into subsequent layers. The system avoids combinatorial explosion by enforcing strict causality chains. Failure modes include data drift, incorrect signal resolution, and layer dependency collapse. Dualities emerge between offensive and defensive layers, e.g., L03 vs L04, which must remain orthogonal to prevent spurious correlation. Temporal consistency is enforced through validation schemas ensuring logical coherence across layers.
